title: Mild Hybrid 48V System — 48V battery state-of-charge low (P15A0-EXT)
shortDescription: 48V mild hybrid system fault: 48V battery state-of-charge low. Stored as P15A0-EXT.
fullDescription: Mild hybrid systems use a belt-driven 48V starter-generator (BSG / ISG) and a small lithium-ion battery to provide regenerative braking, engine off-coast, and torque assist. 48V battery state-of-charge low. Stored as P15A0-EXT. Hybrid functions disable but the engine continues to run on its conventional 12V system.
safetyImpact: Hybrid features (auto stop-start, torque assist, regen) disabled. Engine and conventional electrical operate normally.

causes.cause: Belt tensioner or belt slip on BSG

fixSteps.title: Scan Hybrid Module
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM scan tool to read 48V battery, BSG, and DC-DC data; check for under/over-voltage codes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Belt & Tensioner
fixSteps.instruction: Check BSG belt for cracks and proper tension; replace tensioner if hydraulic damper is leaking.

fixSteps.title: Test 48V Battery
fixSteps.instruction: Capacity test pack; check coolant level and pump for liquid-cooled designs.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty 48V Component
fixSteps.instruction: Follow OEM lockout / safety procedure for 48V before replacing BSG, battery, or DC-DC converter.

faq.a: 48V is below the 60V high-voltage threshold but still requires care — short circuits cause severe arcing.

faq.q: Can I drive with this fault?
faq.a: Yes — the engine and 12V system are independent. Fuel economy will drop a few percent.

title: HV Battery Temperature — Hybrid battery temperature sensor B circuit (P0AAB-EXT)
shortDescription: Hybrid / EV high-voltage battery temperature sensor fault: Hybrid battery temperature sensor B circuit. Stored as P0AAB-EXT.
fullDescription: The high-voltage battery uses multiple temperature sensors to monitor cell, module, and coolant temperatures and to control charging current and cooling fan or chiller activity. Hybrid battery temperature sensor B circuit. Stored as P0AAB-EXT. A failed sensor causes derate or refusal to fast-charge.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and limited charge rate to protect cells from overheating; vehicle remains drivable.

causes.cause: Loose or corroded sensor harness inside battery pack

symptoms: Cabin heat from battery cooling fan

fixSteps.title: Scan BMS Data
fixSteps.instruction: Read each cell-group temperature; identify outliers above or below pack mean by more than spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cooling System
fixSteps.instruction: Check HV coolant level and condition; look for leaks at battery cold plate.

fixSteps.title: Check Sensor Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open service plug and inspect internal pack harness if accessible per OEM service manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor / Module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace temperature sensor or affected battery module; follow OEM HV safety procedure.

faq.a: Pack derates current to protect cells when sensor data is invalid or out of range.
Only certified technicians should open battery enclosures — high voltage can be lethal.

title: Battery Assembly System — Battery assembly contactor A welded (P0EE0-EXT)
shortDescription: High-voltage battery assembly fault: Battery assembly contactor A welded. Stored as P0EE0-EXT.
fullDescription: BAS (Battery Assembly System) codes cover the contactors, pre-charge resistor, isolation monitor, current shunt, and service disconnect inside the high-voltage pack. Battery assembly contactor A welded. Stored as P0EE0-EXT. Most BAS faults open the contactors and disable HV propulsion.
safetyImpact: Loss of HV propulsion possible; in hybrids the engine may continue but EV-only and full-power modes disable.

causes.cause: Isolation fault between HV and chassis

symptoms: Audible contactor click on key cycle

fixSteps.title: Scan HV Module
fixSteps.instruction: Read isolation, contactor state, pre-charge resistor measurements.

fixSteps.title: Verify Service Disconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm orange HV service plug is fully seated and interlock micro-switch closed.

fixSteps.title: Test Contactors
fixSteps.instruction: Measure contactor coil resistance and verify pre-charge sequence with HV-rated meter.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace contactor, pre-charge resistor, or current sensor as instructed; recalibrate BMS.

faq.a: No — only HV-certified technicians with proper PPE should open the high-voltage battery.
Some vehicles will not charge the 12V battery when HV is offline; expect slow no-start later.

title: Intake Air Temperature — Mass / volume air flow sensor B circuit range (P00A1-EXT)
shortDescription: Manifold / intake air temperature sensor fault: Mass / volume air flow sensor B circuit range. Stored as P00A1-EXT.
fullDescription: The intake air temperature sensor reports inlet charge temperature so the PCM can correct fuel, spark, and turbo boost. Mass / volume air flow sensor B circuit range. Stored as P00A1-EXT. Bad data causes hard cold start, knock, or rough idle when wide-open throttle is requested.
safetyImpact: Drivability impacted; in turbo cars boost may be cut to protect the engine from knock under hot conditions.

causes.cause: Sensor coated with oil from PCV

symptoms: MIL on with fuel trim codes

fixSteps.title: Read IAT Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare IAT to ambient at cold start; values should match within a few degrees.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor; check tip for oil, dirt, or damage; clean with electronic cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Test Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe sensor signal and reference; check resistance against OEM temperature curve.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace IAT sensor; clear codes; verify hot/cold readings.

faq.a: Yes — oily intake coats the IAT element and slows response.
Yes — incorrect IAT causes wrong fuel correction and lower mpg.

title: EGR Cooler — EGR cooler bypass valve A control circuit (P00B0-EXT)
shortDescription: Exhaust gas recirculation cooler fault: EGR cooler bypass valve A control circuit. Stored as P00B0-EXT.
fullDescription: The EGR cooler routes hot exhaust gas through a coolant heat exchanger to lower combustion temperatures and NOx. EGR cooler bypass valve A control circuit. Stored as P00B0-EXT. A clogged or leaking cooler causes coolant loss, white smoke, or NOx emission failures.
safetyImpact: Driveable; coolant leak into intake can cause hydrolock or engine damage if ignored.

causes.cause: Cracked EGR cooler core (internal coolant leak)
Failed EGR cooler bypass valve actuator

symptoms: MIL with NOx or EGR codes

fixSteps.title: Pressure Test Cooling System
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize cooling system; watch for drop and inspect intake for coolant residue.

fixSteps.title: Read EGR Data
fixSteps.instruction: Check EGR cooler outlet temp, bypass valve commanded versus actual, and DPF / NOx data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cooler
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooler; visually inspect for cracks, soot blockage, or seal failures.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGR Cooler
fixSteps.instruction: Replace cooler and gaskets; flush coolant; perform regen if applicable.

faq.a: Most common on diesels but many turbo gas engines also have EGR coolers.
Not legally on emissions-controlled vehicles; doing so triggers more codes.
